key_insight: Random, intermittent jet forcing can mix a two-layer stratified fluid while the interface may either sharpen or rise more slowly depending on the density jump.
engineering_relevance: The results inform how turbulent bursts in natural and industrial stratified flows can alter transport, entrainment, and interface stability.
method: Two-layer salt-stratified fluid experiments forced by a randomly actuated synthetic jet array (RASJA).
Interface evolution measured with light attenuation imaging.
Background potential energy used to quantify irreversible mixing and compare cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that interface rise velocity decreases with density jump and that mixing remains irreversible in both regimes, with comparable energy changes.
watch_item: These findings come from laboratory conditions and a specific forcing setup, so scaling them to fully natural flows or different stratifications should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Mixing and sharpening at the interface of a two-layer fluid forced by random jets
